examples.en: I hung the laundry out in the yard.
Hang the wet towels in the bathroom.
I've spread the chili peppers on the roof to dry them.

examples.ko: 비 오기 전에 널어놓은 이불을 걷어야 해요.
examples.en: I have to take in the bedding I hung out before it rains.
Don't leave your clothes lying around anywhere.
They spread all the toys across the living room and play.

explain: 말리려고 펴서 두는 모습이 기본이에요. 빨래는 '널다'가 더 짧고 흔하고, '널어놓다'는 그렇게 해 둔 상태를 강조해요. 장난감처럼 어질러 둘 때도 써요.
explain_en: The basic image is spreading something out to dry. For laundry '널다' is shorter and more common, while '널어놓다' emphasizes leaving it that way. It is also used for leaving things scattered, like toys.

examples.en: I tied the box up tightly with cord.
I bought a bundle of cord.
Tie the newspapers with cord and put them out.
The cord snapped and the load spilled out.
I hung the flowerpot up with cord.
Please cut the cord long.

explain: 짐이나 상자를 묶을 때 쓰는 꼬아 만든 가는 줄이에요. 일상에서는 그냥 '끈'이나 '줄'이라고도 말해요. '노끈으로 묶다'가 가장 자주 나오는 쓰임이에요.
explain_en: It is a thin twisted rope used for tying up loads or boxes. In daily talk people also just say '끈' or '줄'. The most common usage is '노끈으로 묶다'.

examples.en: On summer nights I put up a mosquito net and sleep.
The windows of the country house have mosquito netting.
There's a hole in the mosquito net, so mosquitoes get in.

examples.ko: 캠핑할 때 텐트 안에 모기장을 달았어요.
examples.en: When we went camping, I hung a mosquito net inside the tent.

examples.ko: 모기장 덕분에 밤새 한 번도 안 물렸어요.
examples.en: Thanks to the mosquito net, I didn't get bitten even once all night.

examples.ko: 아이 침대 위에 모기장을 걸어 줬어요.
examples.en: I hung a mosquito net over the child's bed.

explain: 자는 곳을 둘러싸서 모기를 막는 그물이에요. '모기장을 치다', '모기장을 걸다'처럼 말해요. 창문에 붙이는 망은 보통 '방충망'이라고 해요.
explain_en: This is a net that surrounds a sleeping area to keep mosquitoes out. You say '모기장을 치다' or '모기장을 걸다'. The screen fixed to a window is usually called '방충망'.

examples.ko: 문고리가 헐거워서 문이 잘 안 잠겨요.
examples.en: The door handle is loose, so the door doesn't lock well.
I grabbed the doorknob and slowly opened the door.
I hung my bag on the doorknob.
The doorknob is placed too high for a child.
I went to the hardware store to swap in a new door handle.

examples.ko: 문고리는 돌려도 열리지 않아서 열쇠를 찾았어요.
examples.en: The door wouldn't open even when I turned the handle, so I looked for the key.

explain: 문을 열고 닫을 때 잡는 부분이에요. 일상에서는 '문손잡이'나 '손잡이'도 비슷하게 써요.
explain_en: It's the part you hold to open and close a door. In daily talk, '문손잡이' or just '손잡이' are used in a similar way.

examples.ko: 여름이 오기 전에 창문에 방충망을 달았어요.
examples.en: Before summer came, I put a screen on the window.

examples.ko: 창문을 열어 두면 벌레가 들어오니까 방충망을 꼭 닫아 주세요.
examples.en: Bugs come in if the window is open, so please be sure to close the screen.
The screen is torn, so mosquitoes come in.
Cleaning the screen is easy with a damp cloth.
The screen got a hole, so I replaced it.
I only feel at ease once I close the balcony screen too.

explain: 창문과 문에 붙박이로 달아 두는 망이에요. '모기장'은 침대나 텐트 위에 치는 천이라 달라요. 보통 '방충망을 달다·닫다·바꾸다'라고 말해요.
explain_en: It is the mesh fixed on windows and doors. A '모기장' is different: it is a net hung over a bed or tent. People usually say '방충망을 달다', '닫다' or '바꾸다'.

examples.en: Grandmother came with clothes wrapped in a cloth bundle.

examples.ko: 장사꾼이 보따리를 풀어 물건을 보여 줬어요.
examples.en: The peddler untied his bundle and showed his goods.
While moving I tied the small things up in a bundle.
I met a traveling peddler at the market.

examples.ko: 보따리가 너무 무거워서 들 수 없었어요.
examples.en: The bundle was too heavy to lift.
After the trip I came back with a bundle full of gifts.

explain: 보따리는 천으로 물건을 싸서 묶은 짐이에요. 옛날에는 가방 대신 썼고, 지금도 '보따리 장수'나 '이야기 보따리'처럼 남아 있어요. 등에 지는 것은 '봇짐'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: Grandfather started to unpack his bag of old stories.
phrases.nuance_ko: 재미있는 이야기를 많이 꺼내 놓을 때 써요. 이야기가 가득 든 보따리를 푸는 모습에서 나온 비유예요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone starts telling lots of interesting stories. It comes from the image of untying a bundle full of stories.

explain_en: A 보따리 is a load wrapped in cloth and tied. People used it instead of a bag in the past, and it survives in '보따리 장수' (traveling peddler) and '이야기 보따리' (bag of stories). One carried on the back is a '봇짐'.

examples.en: I glued the broken cup with glue.
Glue got on my hand and won't come off.
I applied glue to the sole of the shoe.
The glue smell is too strong.
This glue sticks well to metal too.
Please keep the child from touching the glue.

explain: 한국에서는 강한 접착제를 두루 '본드'라고 불러요. 종이나 가벼운 것은 '풀'로 붙이고, 플라스틱·가죽·신발처럼 튼튼하게 붙여야 할 때 '본드'를 써요. 아주 빨리 붙는 것은 '순간접착제'라고 해서 구분해요.
explain_en: In Korea, 본드 is used for strong adhesive in general. Paper and light items are stuck with 풀 (paste); 본드 is for things that must hold firmly, like plastic, leather, or shoes. The very fast-bonding kind is called 순간접착제 (superglue), which is a separate word.

examples.en: There is an emergency bell in the hallway, so press it if you are in danger.

examples.ko: 화재 훈련 중에 갑자기 비상벨이 울렸어요.
examples.en: The alarm bell suddenly rang during the fire drill.

examples.ko: 화장실 안에 비상벨이 있는 걸 몰랐어요.
examples.en: I didn't know there was an emergency bell inside the restroom.

examples.ko: 누가 장난으로 비상벨을 눌러서 다들 놀랐어요.
examples.en: Someone pressed the alarm bell as a joke, and everyone was startled.
Every school building has an emergency bell installed.

examples.ko: 비상벨 소리가 들리면 침착하게 밖으로 나가세요.
examples.en: If you hear the alarm bell, calmly go outside.

explain: '비상벨이 울리다, 비상벨을 누르다, 비상벨을 설치하다'처럼 자주 말해요. 벨 자체를 가리키는 말이라서 울리는 소리는 보통 '경보음'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It commonly appears as '비상벨이 울리다' (rings), '비상벨을 누르다' (press) and '비상벨을 설치하다' (install). It names the bell itself, while the sound it makes is usually called '경보음'.

examples.en: I put the bulb into the socket and turned it.
The socket is loose, so the bulb keeps flickering.
The bulb socket was rusty, so I replaced it with a new one.

examples.ko: 소켓에 먼지가 쌓이지 않게 가끔 닦아요.
examples.en: I wipe the socket now and then so dust doesn't build up.

examples.ko: 여행 가는 나라에 맞는 소켓 어댑터를 샀어요.
examples.en: I bought a socket adapter that fits the country I'm traveling to.

examples.ko: 아이가 소켓에 손을 넣지 못하게 덮개를 달았어요.
examples.en: I attached a cover so the child can't put a hand into the socket.

explain: 벽에 있는 전기 구멍은 보통 '콘센트'라고 하고, 소켓은 전구나 부품을 끼우는 받침에 더 가까워요. 그래도 외국 제품 설명에서는 벽 콘센트를 소켓이라고 부르기도 해요. 컴퓨터에서 쓰는 '소켓 통신'도 같은 낱말이에요.
explain_en: The electric hole in a wall is usually called a 콘센트, while 소켓 is closer to the base where you fit a bulb or a part. Still, foreign product descriptions sometimes call a wall outlet a 소켓. The 소켓 in computer 소켓 통신 (socket communication) is the same word.

en: the former home of a married woman

examples.en: I went to my parents' home for the holiday and rested.
My parents' home is close, so I stop by often.
The married daughter came to visit her parents' home.
There is a persimmon tree in the yard of my parents' home.
They packed lots of side dishes for me at my parents' home.
The new bride missed her parents' home and cried in secret.

explain: 결혼한 여자가 자기 부모님이 사는 집을 말해요. 짧게 '친정'이라고도 하고, 보통 '친정에 가다'처럼 써요. 남편 부모님 집은 '시댁'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It is the home of a married woman's own parents. It is often shortened to '친정', as in '친정에 가다'. Her husband's parents' home is '시댁'.

examples.en: The kids upstairs stomp around all day.
Please don't stomp; walk gently.
I woke up because of a banging sound at night.

examples.ko: 동생이 화가 나서 문을 쿵쾅거리며 나갔어요.
examples.en: My younger sibling got angry and went out banging the doors.
There has been banging since morning because of construction, so it's noisy.
I was so nervous that my heart pounded.

explain: '쿵쿵'보다 크고 거친 소리가 여러 번 이어질 때 써요. 발소리, 문 닫는 소리, 공사 소리뿐 아니라 '가슴이 쿵쾅거리다'처럼 심장이 세게 뛸 때도 써요. 층간 소음 이야기에서 자주 들려요.
explain_en: Use it when loud, rough thuds repeat, a bit stronger than '쿵쿵'. It fits footsteps, slamming doors and construction, and also a heart pounding hard as in '가슴이 쿵쾅거리다'. You often hear it in talk about noise from upstairs neighbors.

examples.ko: 여론 조사에서는 앞섰지만 실제 당선 여부는 투표함을 열어 봐야 알아요.
examples.en: He led in the polls, but we can only know if he really wins once the ballot box is opened.

examples.ko: 투표함을 열기 전까지 가결 여부는 아무도 알 수 없었어요.
examples.en: Until the ballot box was opened, nobody could know whether it would pass.
I put my ballot in the ballot box and came out.
When voting ended, they moved the ballot boxes to the counting hall.

examples.ko: 투표함 앞에 사람들이 줄을 서 있어요.
examples.en: People are lined up in front of the ballot box.
We made a simple ballot box in the classroom.

explain: 투표용지를 넣는 상자예요. 뉴스에서 '투표함을 열어 봐야 안다'처럼 결과를 알기 전까지는 모른다는 뜻으로도 자주 말해요. 개표는 '투표함을 열고 표를 세는 일'이에요.
explain_en: This is the box where ballots are put. In the news, 'we have to open the ballot box to know' is often used to mean you can't know the result until it's counted. '개표' is opening the box and counting the votes.

examples.en: I bought a fly swatter to catch flies.
Do you know where the fly swatter is?

examples.ko: 여름이 되면 집집마다 파리채가 하나씩 있어요.
examples.en: When summer comes, every house has a fly swatter.
I tried to swat a mosquito with the fly swatter and broke a cup.
Grandma went to the kitchen holding a fly swatter.

examples.ko: 이 파리채는 손잡이가 길어서 쓰기 편해요.
examples.en: This fly swatter has a long handle, so it's easy to use.

explain: '파리'에 도구를 뜻하는 '채'가 붙은 말이에요. 파리뿐 아니라 모기나 벌레를 잡을 때도 써요. 보통 '파리채로 때리다/잡다'처럼 말해요.
explain_en: It combines '파리' (fly) with '채', a word for a handheld tool. People also use it for mosquitoes and other bugs. You say '파리채로 때리다/잡다'.

examples.en: An excavator is digging the ground at the construction site.

examples.ko: 포클레인 소리 때문에 낮잠을 못 잤어요.
examples.en: I couldn't nap because of the excavator noise.
My father works driving an excavator.

examples.ko: 길 옆에 큰 포클레인 한 대가 서 있어요.
examples.en: A big excavator is parked beside the road.

examples.ko: 포클레인으로 파면 하루 만에 끝날 거예요.
examples.en: If we dig with an excavator, it will be done in a day.

examples.ko: 어린 아들이 장난감 포클레인만 가지고 놀아요.
examples.en: My little son only plays with his toy excavator.

explain: 공식적인 글에서는 '굴착기'라고 하고, 말할 때는 '포클레인'이라고 하는 사람이 많아요. 땅을 파는 기계라서 '포클레인으로 파다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: In formal writing the word is '굴착기', but many people say '포클레인' when they talk. Since it is a digging machine, it goes naturally with phrases like '포클레인으로 파다' (to dig with an excavator).

examples.en: The fire alarm suddenly went off and startled me.
Every building must install a fire alarm.
Please check the fire alarm battery.
Fire alarms are usually attached to the ceiling.
A strange sound is coming from the fire alarm.
We started the evacuation drill with the fire alarm.

explain: 불이 났을 때 소리로 알려 주는 기계예요. '화재경보기가 울리다'처럼 '울리다'와 같이 쓰는 경우가 많아요. 건물 안전 안내문에서 자주 볼 수 있어요.
explain_en: It is a device that warns of fire with a sound. It usually pairs with '울리다', as in '화재경보기가 울리다'. You often see it in building safety notices.
